ne-rg-1730072715.w: A line of rugged reddish hills rising sharply from the flat Punjab plain, south of Islamabad and the Potohar plateau.
f: A local legend says the salt was discovered when horses of Alexander the Great's army licked the rocks.
The Katas Raj temples in the range surround a sacred pond.

q.q: What is mined at Khewra in the Salt Range?

ne-rg-1730072723.t: A snowy ridge beside the windy Dzungarian Gate
ne-rg-1730072723.s: The wild ancestors of the orchard apple still grow on these slopes. The Dzungarian Alatau rises as a long, snowy barrier on the border of Kazakhstan and China, with glaciers on its crest and forests of wild apple and spruce below. At its north-eastern end lies the Dzungarian Gate, a narrow pass famous for fierce winds, long used by nomads and caravans.
ne-rg-1730072723.w: A long snowy ridge with glaciers on the Kazakhstan–China border, with the lakes Alakol and Balkhash to the north and west.
f: In Kazakh the range is called Zhetysu Alatau, after the 'land of seven rivers' at its foot.
Winds in the Dzungarian Gate can reach hurricane strength.

q.q: What is the windy pass at the end of the Dzungarian Alatau called?

ne-rg-1730072741.t: A long mountain spine through Iran's desert heart
ne-rg-1730072741.s: Snow on these bare ridges has kept desert cities alive for centuries, its meltwater carried by qanats, underground channels dug by hand. The Kuhrud range runs across Iran for hundreds of kilometres, from near Qom towards Kerman, inland from the higher Zagros. Kashan and Yazd grew at its feet, and east of it the land falls away to the great central deserts.
ne-rg-1730072741.w: Long, bare, parallel ridges running north-west to south-east across central Iran, with desert basins on either side.
f: Shir Kuh, near Yazd, is the range's highest peak at over 4,000 m.
The Persian qanat system is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

q.q: What are Iran's ancient underground water channels called?

Q1517159.t: A plateau cut by a canyon of mud-brick towns
Q1517159.s: Hundreds of mud-brick tower houses, packed inside the walls of Shibam, earned this town the nickname 'Manhattan of the desert'. It stands on the floor of Wadi Hadramawt, a deep, winding canyon slashed into the flat, stony Jol plateau of eastern Yemen. The plateau looks like crumpled brown paper; the valley floor is a green ribbon of palms and fields.
Q1517159.w: A flat brown, deeply dissected plateau with a long green valley winding through it from west to east, inland from the Arabian Sea.
f: Shibam's mud-brick tower houses rise up to about 30 m.
Shibam became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1982.

q.q: Roughly how tall are Shibam's tallest tower houses?

Q1352266.t: Tundra peninsula beside a strait named for two ships
Q1352266.s: Between the Arctic mainland and Baffin Island, the Melville Peninsula reaches north into the ice-choked channels of Nunavut. It is a broad land of low tundra hills, lakes and rocky coast, frozen for most of the year. Its northern tip faces the Fury and Hecla Strait, named by William Parry after his two ships, which spent two winters nearby searching for the Northwest Passage.
Q1352266.w: A broad, lake-dotted tundra peninsula reaching north, with Foxe Basin to the east and a narrow strait at its northern tip.
f: The Inuit community of Igloolik lies on a small island just off its north-eastern coast.
Parry's ships HMS Fury and HMS Hecla wintered here in 1821–23.

q.q: What is the Fury and Hecla Strait named after?

Q151559.t: Where the Appalachians end at the Gulf of St. Lawrence
Q151559.s: The Gaspé Peninsula pushes east into the Gulf of St. Lawrence, a wild, forested land where the Appalachian Mountains finally meet the sea. Its interior is filled by the Chic-Chocs, rounded summits above 1,200 m that hold snow well into spring. In 1534 Jacques Cartier landed in Gaspé Bay and raised a cross, claiming the land for France.
Q151559.w: A forested peninsula jutting east into the Gulf of St. Lawrence, with rounded mountains inland and a rocky coast ending in cliffs.
f: Gaspé comes from a Mi'kmaq word meaning 'land's end'.
Percé Rock, a limestone ridge pierced by an arch, stands just off the peninsula's tip.
Mont Jacques-Cartier, about 1,270 m, is the highest peak of the Chic-Chocs.

q.q: What does the Mi'kmaq word behind the name Gaspé mean?

ne-rg-1730072887.t: Remote tundra between the Ob and the Yenisei
ne-rg-1730072887.s: Nenets herders still lead their reindeer across this roadless tundra, as their ancestors did for centuries. The Gyda Peninsula stretches north into the Kara Sea between the mouths of two Siberian giants, the Ob and the Yenisei: a flat land of countless lakes and winding rivers, frozen for three-quarters of the year.
ne-rg-1730072887.w: Flat tundra riddled with lakes and winding rivers, between two wide gulfs opening north into the Kara Sea.
f: The Gydan Nature Reserve, created in 1996, protects part of the peninsula's Arctic coast.
The peninsula lies almost entirely north of the Arctic Circle.

q.q: Which people herd reindeer across the Gyda Peninsula?

ne-rg-1730072935.t: A cool plateau ending in a dizzying escarpment
ne-rg-1730072935.s: At the Tundavala Gap the ground simply ends: cliffs drop about 1,000 m from the Huíla Plateau towards Angola's coastal plain. The plateau itself is a cool upland around 1,800 m high, home to the city of Lubango. Not far away, the Serra da Leba road descends the same escarpment in a famous tangle of hairpin bends.
ne-rg-1730072935.w: A high green plateau ending in a sheer western escarpment, with hazy dry lowlands stretching towards the coast below.
f: Lubango, the plateau's main city, lies at about 1,760 m.
The dry lowlands below the escarpment form the northern end of the Namib Desert.

q.q: Which Angolan city lies on the Huíla Plateau?

ne-rg-1730072967.t: Sandstone gorges and striped domes in the far north-west
ne-rg-1730072967.s: The Kimberley Plateau is a rugged sandstone upland in the far north-west of Australia, cut by gorges and waterfalls that roar in the wet season and fall silent in the dry. Its rock shelters hold some of the oldest and most elaborate rock art on the continent. On the plateau's south-eastern edge, the Bungle Bungle Range rises in orange-and-black striped beehive domes.
ne-rg-1730072967.w: Rugged red sandstone uplands cut by deep green gorges in Australia's far north-west, with few roads and almost no towns.
f: Purnululu National Park, home of the Bungle Bungles, became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2003.
The Gibb River Road, a famous dirt track, crosses the region for about 660 km.
The Gwion Gwion paintings show slender, elegant human figures.

q.q: What are the Bungle Bungles famous for?
